standard.title: Cultural, religious and social groups and identity
standard.description: diversity of cultural, religious and/or social groups to which they and others in the community belong, and their importance to identity
standard.strand: Knowledge and Understanding — Civics and Citizenship/History
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3K02): Students explored significant Australian events, symbols and identity. From Foundation-Y2: Students explored celebrations, family structures and community connections.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the diversity of cultural, religious and social groups to which they and others belong and describe their importance to identity.

nodes.label: Groups people belong to
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the different social, cultural and religious groups they and others in their community belong to and describe what makes them feel part of each group.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three groups they belong to and describe what makes them feel part of each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify diversity through different social, cultural and religious groups students belong to; describe what creates belonging; list and compare different beliefs, traditions and symbols used by different groups.
wider: Compare how belonging to different groups simultaneously can sometimes create tensions or enrich identity
Investigate how immigration has diversified the cultural groups present in the local community
nodes.hinge_reason: Students need to identify and describe the groups they belong to before they can analyse how those groups shape identity — the identity analysis in Node 2 requires this foundation.

response_modes.reason: Students benefit from exploring the full range of group types (cultural, religious, interest, community) before analysing any in depth.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Classroom diversity means groups represented will vary significantly — authentic sharing creates genuine cross-cultural understanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least three groups they belong to
Describes what creates belonging in at least one group

nodes.label: Groups and identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how membership of groups shapes identity, including how First Nations Australian identity is shaped by Country/Place, language and knowledge traditions.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least one group shapes their own identity.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise that identity is shaped by membership of multiple groups; recognise that First Nations Australian identity is specifically shaped by Country/Place, language and knowledge traditions.
wider: Compare how identity is shaped by voluntary groups (interest groups) and ascribed groups (cultural, religious, national) and discuss differences
Investigate how First Nations Australian language and knowledge traditions shape identity and what is at risk when these traditions are not maintained

response_modes.reason: The breadth of group types that shape identity — including First Nations groups — gives richest understanding of identity as constructed and multiple.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding identity as shaped by multiple group memberships (not singular) is a key civic and personal development insight — rich widening here builds lifelong intercultural capability.
success_criteria: Explains how at least one group shapes their identity
Recognises that First Nations Australian identity is specifically shaped by Country/Place, language and knowledge traditions
